status: block complete (ensemble probe at k=5). 8 distinct verified 5-colourings obtained; intersection leaves 30395 untested candidate pairs; one pre-registered survivor tested and returned SAT. NO certification of the no-forced-equality statement, because the survivor set is not empty. Two overclaims withdrawn.
summary: Ran the bounded ensemble: 8 distinct 5-colourings of the validated 553-vertex point set, each verified against all 2722 edges (0 monochromatic), each a genuinely different PARTITION (canonical first-occurrence relabelling plus symmetry breaking, so colour permutations cannot masquerade as diversity). Intersecting the same-colour non-adjacent pair sets eliminated 344 of 30739 pairs and left 30395 survivors. Pair (0,39) is among the eliminated, agreeing with the supervisor's independent check. Since survivors remain, there is NO certificate that forced equalities are absent: the 30395 are untested candidates, not forcing evidence. One pre-registered survivor, pair (0,50), was tested with the combinatorial disequality edge and returned SAT with an independently re-checked colouring (c(0)=1, c(50)=0). The diversification was poor: partitions differ from the first in only 192-664 of ~30700 pairs, so block-one-partition-at-a-time yields near-duplicates and cannot shrink the survivor set quickly. Withdrew the claim that solver speed or the 30703 count proves a large solution space, and the claim that no realisation can ever enforce a colour disequality.
verified_results: GRADE [A] Eight distinct verified 5-colourings of the 553-vertex point set. Each checked against all 2722 edges of refs/heule_553.edge by a code path that reads the edge list directly: 0 monochromatic edges, exactly 5 colours used. Partition distinctness is machine-checked, not assumed: every solution is canonically relabelled by order of first appearance, so two witnesses are the same partition iff their canonical vectors are equal; all 8 canonical vectors differ.

GRADE [A] Intersection result: S* = 30395 survivors, 344 pairs eliminated, from 30739 same-colour non-adjacent pairs in witness 0. The eliminated pairs are published with the witness index that separates each, in certs/ensemble_eliminated.txt (344 lines). The full survivor list and all 8 canonical witnesses are in certs/ensemble_k5.json.

GRADE [A] Pair (0,39), ruled out by the supervisor, is ELIMINATED by this ensemble rather than merely excluded: it is not in the survivor set, so an independently verified colouring separates it. Consistent with the supervisor's check.

GRADE [A] Pre-registered single survivor test: pair (0,50) (largest common-neighbour count among survivors, then smallest i, j). G + pq is 5-colourable; the witness was re-checked against all 2722 edges with 0 monochromatic edges, c(0)=1 and c(50)=0, and (0,50) confirmed not to be an original edge. Verdict SAT, so this pair is not forced equal at k=5 either.
GRADE [A] Whole experiment: one process, 1.11 s against the 60 s cap, including generation of all 8 witnesses, all solver calls and all witness checks. Checkpointed JSON after every witness.

GRADE [A]+[P] Diversification mechanism corrected, with the failed version preserved. Run 1 blocked the canonical ASSIGNMENT, which a relabelled copy of the same partition evades; it produced 1 witness and re-tested the excluded pair (0,39). Kept as certs/ensemble_k5_RUN1_buggy.json. The fix adds first-occurrence symmetry breaking (c(0)=0; for v>0 and t in 1..4, c(v)!=t or some u<v has c(u)=t-1), which does not change the set of partitions represented and makes each partition have exactly one admissible assignment, so blocking an assignment blocks a partition.

GRADE [A] Measured diversity, published so the ensemble is not over-credited: witnesses 1-7 differ from witness 0 in only 230, 192, 422, 243, 472, 435, 664 vertex-pairs respectively, out of roughly 30700 same-colour pairs. The ensemble is therefore highly correlated and eliminated about 1.1% of candidate pairs.

GRADE [C] Inherited and kept separate: the 553-vertex 4-UNSAT control with drat-trim-verified DRAT certificate; the block-1 colouring counts and the iff-k=3 diamond proposition; Theorems A, B, C in GLUING.md with corrected non-adjacent-pair count 149906.
conjectures: Blocking one partition at a time returns near-duplicate colourings (measured: under 3% of pair structure changes per step), so this diversification cannot approach a zero survivor set in any useful number of solves. A diversity-directed ensemble is needed: either maximise pairwise distance between witnesses explicitly, or force designated vertex pairs apart, so that each new witness separates many surviving pairs rather than a few hundred.
Whether any non-adjacent pair of this point set is forced equal at k=5 remains OPEN. 30395 candidates survive and exactly one of them has been tested; that is no evidence either way about the rest.

The constraint c(p) != c(q) for a pair at distance != 1 is not a unit edge in this embedding, but it is NOT established to be geometrically unrealisable: extra vertices at unit distance from p and q could in principle shrink the two palettes until they are disjoint, as the diamond forces an equality at k=3 with no non-unit edge.

failed_routes: The ensemble as first implemented was not a valid diversification: blocking the canonical assignment does not block the partition, because a colour-permuted copy is a different assignment. Detected by the run itself (1 witness instead of 8). Fixed with first-occurrence symmetry breaking; failed run preserved rather than deleted.

The corrected ensemble is valid but too correlated to be decisive: 344 of 30739 pairs eliminated, 30395 survivors. The zero-survivor certification criterion was NOT met, so no certified statement about forced equalities at k=5 is claimed.

Withdrawn: the inference that a fast solve or the 30703 same-colour count demonstrates a large solution space. Neither measures the space, and the measured near-duplication of witnesses points the other way about local structure.

Withdrawn: the sentence 'no unit-distance realisation can enforce c(p) != c(q)'. In this embedding pq is not a unit edge, but geometry plus additional vertices can in principle enforce the disequality; corrected in both EXPERIMENT-disequality.md (dated addendum) and GLUING.md (scope note).
Not attempted: scanning all surviving pairs (no exhaustive sweep, per instruction); a DRAT certificate (only needed on UNSAT, which did not arise).
next_step: Replace the weak diversification with a diversity-directed ensemble, still bounded: generate witnesses while requiring each new partition to place a designated pair of vertices into different classes, choosing those pairs from the 30395 survivors, so that each new witness separates a large block of survivors instead of a few hundred. Target is to drive the survivor set to zero, which would then be a finite certificate that no non-adjacent pair of this graph is forced equal at k=5. Track the survivor count per witness and stop at the 60 s cap, reporting partial elimination as inconclusive rather than as a certificate.

escalation.obstacle: Determine whether the 30395 surviving pairs contain a forced equality at k=5, i.e. a pair (p,q) non-adjacent such that every 5-colouring of the 553-vertex point set has c(p)=c(q). One survivor of the 30395 has been tested and returns SAT; the rest are untested.
escalation.definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. A pair is forced equal at k if G is k-colourable and G plus the edge pq is not. Diamond: K_4 minus an edge, vertices a,b,t1,t2, edges ab, at1, at2, bt1, bt2, |t1-t2| = sqrt3.
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates (Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11)); complete finite graph; no measurability, periodicity or lattice hypothesis; k = 5.
escalation.attempted_approaches: Single-pair disequality probe (SAT, pair (0,39), superseded); block-one-partition ensemble of 8 witnesses with partition-exact blocking (344 eliminated, 30395 survivors, one survivor tested SAT); clique-sum and palette-excluder theorems (Theorems A and B) which rule out the direct common-neighbour mechanism for k >= 4.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a diversity-directed ensemble that drives the survivor set to zero, giving a finite checkable certificate that this particular graph has no forced equality at k = 5, or a theorem bounding how many witnesses are needed to separate all 149906 non-adjacent pairs in terms of the number of colour classes and their sizes, together with an explicit example showing the bound is attained or showing why the counting argument fails.
